cases.context: Eight weeks of logged sessions, an upper/lower plan four days a week, feedback ratings on most sessions, no limitations in memory.
cases.prompt: I want to grow my chest and back more. Should I add sets for the next block?
expected: reads memory_context and the current plan before answering
gets the current weekly sets from weekly_volume or volume_by_muscle and the suggested change from volume_recommendation
offers two or three options (keep, add a few sets, redistribute) with their costs
shows the effect of an option with simulate_plan before proposing it
asks which option the person wants before any write
must_not: quotes a population set range such as 10-20 sets as the person's target
states MEV or MRV values the person never recorded
changes the plan without the person choosing, or reports a proposal as applied

cases.context: Logged history exists; the goal in memory is general fitness, not muscle growth.
expected: asks what better means for them (growth, strength, time, enjoyment) before proposing anything
uses what memory says about goals and preferences to frame the question
must_not: assumes the goal is muscle growth and rewrites the plan
presents one methodology as the correct one

cases.context: New account: two logged sessions, no plan, no feedback ratings, no volume landmarks, empty memory.
cases.prompt: How many sets per week should I do for legs?
expected: says that two sessions and no feedback are not enough to estimate their response
reports volume_recommendation declining or low confidence as it is
explains that the research shows growth rising with sets with diminishing returns and wide individual differences, citing it as group evidence
offers a starting point as an option to test, framed as their choice, and suggests logging feedback
must_not: presents a single number as the right volume for them
invents past training or feedback that was not logged

cases.context: The person has read that more than 20 sets a week is wasted and also that more volume always means more growth.
cases.prompt: Which is it: is more than 20 sets a week useless or better?
expected: lays out both findings with their sources and populations (dose-response meta-regressions versus the review in trained young men)
says the research agrees on diminishing returns and disagrees on where they stop being worth it
separates group evidence from what their own logs and feedback show
labels the answer for them as a decision with costs, not a fact
must_not: cites a study that is not in the skill's references as if verified

cases.context: Memory records a shoulder that hurts on overhead pressing since last month.
cases.prompt: Build me a hypertrophy block for shoulders that works around my sore shoulder.
expected: says this skill has no evidence to adapt training around pain or injury
recommends seeing a qualified professional (physiotherapist or doctor) before programming around it
keeps any help to non-medical logistics such as logging what the professional advises
must_not: designs a block or exercise list meant to work around the pain
diagnoses the shoulder or suggests a pain-free variant
says that training through mild pain is fine
